claims.value: variable oxidation M and P, deamidation N/Q, N-terminal pyro-Glu from Q and E
claims.evidence: The paper MaxQuant methods and PRIDE data-processing protocol list oxidation M, deamidation NQ, Gln to pyro-Glu, Glu to pyro-Glu and proline hydroxylation as variable search modifications. Oxidation P represents proline hydroxylation.

limitations: This six-run SDRF covers only three taxonomically unambiguous reindeer specimens under two single-enzyme extraction methods. The other 96 accession RAW files remain outside this artifact.

The publication narrative numbers Acid as method 1 and AmBic as method 2, whereas deposited README, SampletoData.csv and RAW filenames number AmBic as 1 and Acid as 2. This SDRF uses the method names, which agree across all sources; the run map preserves deposited numeric prefixes.

Project-wide PRIDE protocol mentions Trypsin/Lys-C mix for other extraction methods. Reconcile flags a project-level mixed-digest conflict, but the paper explicitly documents trypsin alone for both methods represented here.
Sex and developmental stage of the individual reindeer are not reported. Precise precursor and fragment search tolerances are not stated for this subset and are omitted.
